title: Zork I
build: Infocom's original disk, release 15, serial number UG3AU5: Zork I r15-UG3AU5.woz (SHA-1 f76f5449...d87a2) from archive.org's A Woz A Day collection, item wozaday_Zork_I_r15; analysed at the Z-machine's start, when the interpreter has read the story's first $48 pages (orientation.md)

credits.role: an author of the game (the disk's WOZ metadata; archive.org's description of the disk)
an author of the game (the disk's WOZ metadata; archive.org's description of the disk)

tools.emulator: Apple2TS 3.7.0 (git c900979), bundled by the kit into its server (kit/apple2), a 128K enhanced Apple IIe; check-emulator 42 passed, 0 failed, on 19 October 2026
tools.disassembler: regenerator2000 0.9.20 in its Apple II mode, driven through kit/apple2/r2000.py
tools.host: Linux 6.18 x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04, a hosted cloud session with no display

accuracy.note: 60 of the 330 comments written by hand and 20 of the 597 a decoder of the story file wrote; seven by hand wrong in a detail, all corrected with the three comments that said the same

exclude: the line buffer GETLN fills and the interpreter prints from, and the Z-machine's stack, which grows down from $03E7 (runtime state)

the text screen, which at the Z-machine's start holds only spaces and the `Apple //e` line the ROM printed at power-on, and its screen holes, where the disk routines keep each drive's head position ($0478, $04F8) (not the game's)
the four tables of which story page is in which buffer, built at start-up over the loader (runtime state)
the disk routines' nibble buffers, holding whatever sector was read last (runtime state)
the 76 page buffers, filled from the disk as the story needs its pages (runtime state; empty at the Z-machine's start)
extra: the story's resident part: its first $48 pages, read from the disk at start-up and kept, which nothing in the 6502 code refers to by address
virtual: the story's other 248 pages, story $04800-$13FFF, with most of its routines and most of its text, which the interpreter reads from the disk one page at a time into its page buffers at $7400-$BFFF as the Z-machine needs them
